# s394 — foreign_worktree warns falsely when GIT_DIR is set, as in a merge driver

**Findings:** ork S87 landing, 2026-10-25 · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-10-26** — Ready for review: foreign_worktree probes slicer's code dir without GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_COMMON_DIR (vcs._code_probe_env, threaded through git_common_dir and _current_worktree via an optional env); the project probe keeps the caller's env. Tests: test_GitDirSetForAnotherRepo_NoWarning, test_SiblingWorktreeGitEnvSet_Warns; full suite OK; reviewer confirmed with a real merge driver in a linked worktree.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

When git runs slicer's merge driver (`slicer merge-index %O %A %B`) during `git -C ork/.worktrees/s87 merge main`, slicer printed: "running code from .../slicer/src/slicer, but this project is .../ork/.worktrees/s87 -- a different worktree of the same repo". ork and slicer are different repos. Reproduced on 2026-10-25 without a merge: `GIT_DIR=/path/to/ork/.git slicer --root /path/to/ork check` prints the warning, while the same command without GIT_DIR does not. `foreign_worktree` (src/slicer/vcs.py:538-572) calls `git_common_dir` (src/slicer/vcs.py:496) for the code dir, and with GIT_DIR in the environment git answers for the project's repo, not slicer's, so both common dirs match. The merge result was correct; the line is noise in every merge of a worktree branch that has slicer's drivers.

## Files

- `src/slicer/vcs.py:496-508` (git_common_dir) and `src/slicer/vcs.py:538-572` (foreign_worktree): probe the code dir with the discovery variables (`_DISCOVERY_ENV`, src/slicer/vcs.py:88) removed from the environment.

## Failing tests

- `test_foreignWorktree_gitDirSetForAnotherRepo_returnsNone`: with GIT_DIR pointing at an unrelated repo, no warning.
- The existing same-repo different-worktree case still warns.

## Implement

Strip GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_COMMON_DIR only for the code-dir probe; the project probe keeps the caller's environment.

## Check

`python3 tests/affected.py --run`; `slicer check`.
